name: Aerospace Engineering
notes: Four courses. Non-ME majors take three aerospace core courses and one mechanical engineering course; ME majors take all four from the aerospace core list.
Open to all majors and particularly compatible with mechanical engineering, physics, optical engineering, chemical engineering, and electrical and computer engineering.

SENIOR DESIGN: students not taking a senior design course as part of their major must take ME 205 (Advanced Mechanical Design) and complete the aerospace design project in that class. The instructor issues a letter certifying the project - that is also what makes ME 205 count as an aerospace core course.
Up to two courses from the minor can be used toward a separate major or minor - EXCEPT for the mechanical engineering major, which may overlap only one course.
Students cannot declare a minor until accepted into a major, and cannot elect the satisfactory/fail option for minor courses.
Contact Professor John Lambropoulos, who evaluates and manages all ME minors, before declaring.

requirementGroups.label: Three aerospace core courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Aerospace Core Courses. At least three of the following courses*: ME 205: Advanced Mechanical Design**; ME 214/407: Advanced Dynamics; ME 222/424: Introduction to Robust Design and Quality Engineering; ME 227/427: Introduction to Aerodynamics; ME 231/431: Feedback Control of Dynamic Systems; ME 232/432: Opto-Mechanical Design; ME 246/446: Aerospace Structures; ME 254/441: Finite Element Methods. *Mechanical engineering majors must choose all four of their minor courses from this list.

requirementGroups.label: One mechanical engineering course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Mechanical Engineering Courses. One of the following*: ME 204: Mechanical Design; ME 213: Mechanical Systems and Vibrations; ME 225: Introduction to Fluid Dynamics; ME 226: Introduction to Solid Mechanics; CHE 268: Fundamentals of Computational Fluid Dynamics; ME 280: Materials Science; ME 436: Compressible Flow; ME 437: Incompressible Flow; ME 439: Turbulence; ME 440: Mechanics of Structures; ME 444: Continuum Mechanics; ME 449: Elasticity; ME 459: Applied Finite Elements; ME 481: Mechanical Properties of Solids. *Mechanical engineering majors must select all four courses from the core aerospace course list.
requirementGroups.note: MECHANICAL ENGINEERING MAJORS take a fourth AEROSPACE CORE course here instead.
